title: Team up GBDTs and DNNs: Advancing Efficient and Effective Tabular Prediction with Tree-hybrid MLPs

problem.claim: Selecting an effective model for a specific tabular dataset is challenging and often requires time-consuming hyperparameter tuning.

gap.claim: Existing back-propagation optimization struggles to efficiently discover well-performing GBDT-like functionality within deep learning models.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Tree-hybrid simple MLP (T-MLP) that combines GBDT feature gating, DNN architecture pruning, model-ensemble ideas, and vanilla back-propagation.
The framework uses a tensorized, rapidly trained GBDT feature gate and a DNN architecture-pruning approach to train a randomly initialized MLP.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present T-MLP as a new framework and algorithm combining the advantages of GBDTs and DNNs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report comprehensive experiments on 88 tabular datasets showing that T-MLP is competitive with extensively tuned DNNs and GBDTs on their respective dominant benchmarks.
The authors report compact model storage and significantly reduced training duration.
The authors report that code and full experiment results are publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tabular prediction is important across applications, while GBDTs and DNNs each perform well on different tabular tasks.
Choosing between model types for a particular dataset is difficult and expensive because it often requires extensive hyperparameter tuning.
Deep learning can represent a well-performing GBDT model, but standard back-propagation may not efficiently find that functionality; GBDT components are described as more adaptable to tabular data.
The paper combines GBDT feature gating, DNN pruning, and back-propagation in the T-MLP framework.
The authors report competitive performance across 88 datasets with compact storage and shorter training duration.

source_observation.claim: The method combines components associated with GBDTs and DNNs to address model-selection difficulty for tabular data.

interpretation.claim: Hybridizing complementary inductive biases and optimization mechanisms may reduce dependence on choosing one model family in advance.

application.claim: For tabular prediction systems, consider combining tree-derived feature gating with neural architecture and optimization components.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which datasets, task conditions, or implementation settings limit the reported advantage.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the 88 datasets, baselines, metrics, or statistical comparisons.
The abstract does not provide ablation results or implementation details.
The abstract does not quantify storage reduction or training-duration reduction.
